decisions.boundary_condition: Applies only to hotel room price tradeoffs. It does not establish a fixed reusable nightly budget such as $150, and it does not automatically apply to flights, dining, activities, or other travel purchases.
decisions.canonical_value: Prefer the lowest-priced acceptable hotel room when no higher-priority hotel requirement has been stated.
decisions.condition: When comparing or booking hotel rooms and the user has not provided a higher-priority reason to pay more.
decisions.default_action: Prioritize the lowest available acceptable nightly rate and respect any explicitly stated low-price constraint rather than upselling to costlier rooms.
decisions.exception_condition: Do not choose solely by lowest price if the user explicitly requests a costlier room type, property feature, location, quality level, or says they are flexible on price to satisfy another constraint.
decisions.name: Prefer the cheapest acceptable hotel room
decisions.rationale: Multiple hotel-related examples show the user selecting or asking for the cheapest available room or imposing a low nightly-rate constraint. This supports a soft hotel price-sensitivity default, but not a reusable numeric ceiling or a rule that price always overrides stated room, location, or amenity requirements.
